title: Part
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, initiate a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. Within this first face, draw a single loop, and within this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates (0.0183, 0.0183) with a radius of 0.0183 units. After completing the circle, apply a scale factor of 0.0366 to the entire sketch to adjust its size accordingly. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it according to the Euler angles and translating it using the specified translation vector. Finally, extrude the transformed sketch to create a solid body. The extrusion should extend 0.75 units in the direction of the normal without any extrusion in the opposite direction. The resulting shape is a cylindrical object with a small rectangular protrusion at the top. The cylindrical part has a length and width of 0.036585365853658534 units and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circle with the given center and radius
r = r.center(0.0183, 0.0183).circle(0.0183)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0183, 0.0183)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0183)  # Draw a circle with the specified radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder
